passages.provision_quote: It is the policy of the state to do both of the following: (1) Achieve net zero greenhouse gas emissions as soon as possible, but no later than 2045, and to achieve and maintain net negative greenhouse gas emissions thereafter.
passages.note: A declared net-zero emissions policy plus directives to recommend measures and enable carbon capture; it names no energy source and imposes no duty to supply or buy clean energy.

rows.reasoning: AB 1279 (2021-2022), which Muratsuchi authored, declares it the policy of the state to "Achieve net zero greenhouse gas emissions as soon as possible, but no later than 2045" and directs the state board to "identify and recommend measures" and to "Identify and implement a variety of policies and strategies that enable carbon dioxide removal solutions and carbon capture, utilization, and storage technologies in California". An emissions target the state may meet by any means, including carbon capture, names no energy source, so it does not match "Require a shift to clean energy through mandates and firm deadlines"; it also neither funds clean energy, nor cuts permitting red tape and upgrades the grid, nor ends support. It shows only the pro-action side.
needs_source: Assembly floor roll call plus bill text for a California renewable or clean-electricity procurement standard carrying dated binding percentages (a clean-energy supply duty), to test "Require a shift to clean energy through mandates and firm deadlines"

Muratsuchi's own act (authorship, sponsorship or a final-passage vote) on a single-subject clean-energy subsidy, tax credit or public investment programme, to test "Fund clean energy with major subsidies, tax credits, and public investment"
Muratsuchi's own words on whether clean energy should be required or only funded, to separate the rungs on the pro-action side
